correctness.rationale: For every real 0<a,c<1 with a≠c, the norm is a signed-coordinate-invariant polygonal norm. Independently reconstructed a full equivalent quadratic-ellipsoid sandwich: averaging Q over sign changes proves no oblique quadratic form improves distortion; the inner condition is exactly u,v≥1 and A²/u+B²/v≤1 by weighted Cauchy–Schwarz; the outer factor is exactly max(u+a²v,c²u+v) by the four quadrant vertices. If A²+B²≤1 (equivalent to a+c+ac≥1), u=v=1 is coordinatewise minimal. Otherwise the minimizing active-constraint arc has v=B²u/(u−A²), the two costs cross exactly once at explicit (u*,v*), with negative L2 derivative before and positive L1 derivative after; clipping at u=1 or v=1 produces precisely the two endpoint branches. The two infeasible strict conditions cannot coexist under a+c+ac<1 and equality boundaries match. The proof covers all parameter quantifiers and boundaries in its stated open region; no finite computation is used as the general proof.

value.rationale: The extreme points of the convex set of two-dimensional absolute normalized norms constitute a natural canonical two-parameter family; after symmetric and boundary cases are removed, the interior asymmetric case still has a genuine two-dimensional parameter region. The result computes the exact Euclidean Banach–Mazur distance at every interior asymmetric point, with four sharp feasible regions and corresponding optimal ellipsoids. Those two distinct coordinate-tangent phases and their algebraic transitions are not supplied by the inspected old family classification or general ellipse uniqueness. A precise sharp distance and ellipse for a canonical family are independently useful, without requiring a higher-dimensional generalization. This is a natural complete classification, not a renamed special case or arbitrary small numerical instance.
residual_risks: This is a planar family-specific invariant; it does not settle higher-dimensional Banach–Mazur optimization.
Historical priority limitation on an equivalent general closed formula also qualifies value if later found.
